tasks.title: Preserve unknown keys during v1->v2 migration

declaration.objective: v1->v2 config migration preserves all unrelated user-defined keys and does not mutate input

criteria.statement: all unrelated user-defined keys are preserved recursively
the input config object is not mutated
a regression test covers preservation of unknown keys

execution_fit.choice: FIT: verified existing uncommitted fix meets all 5 criteria; can complete claim/verdict/settle
execution_fit.rationale: criteria: all 5 understood and match ISSUE.md; capability: code already present in working tree (cfgmigrate/migrate.py uses copy.deepcopy + pop/setdefault) and appears correct; hardest: confirming no-mutation and recursive independence for nested structures, and that this isn't just a worker claim; evidence: ran full pytest suite (13 passed incl. 3 new regression tests for preserve/nested-independence/no-mutate), and manually reproduced the exact ISSUE.md YAML example confirming output matches expected and input dict is unchanged via deepcopy equality check; not authorised/equipped: will not commit, push, or run tallyback land/settle land without being explicitly asked; stop if: any test fails or manual repro output diverges from ISSUE.md's expected YAML

claims.statement: _v1_to_v2 now deep-copies the input, renames timeout to request_timeout via pop, sets version=2, and defaults plugins; all 5 acceptance criteria (rename, version, recursive preserve, no mutation, regression test) are met and verified

evidence.note: 13 passed, 0 failed: all pre-existing tests plus 3 new regression tests (test_preserves_unknown_keys, test_preserves_nested_unknown_keys_independently, test_does_not_mutate_input)

confidence.rationale: test_renames_timeout_to_request_timeout and manual ISSUE.md repro confirm rename+version; test_preserves_unknown_keys and test_preserves_nested_unknown_keys_independently confirm recursive preservation with independent copies (deepcopy); test_does_not_mutate_input plus manual pre/post equality check confirm the input object is never mutated; the three new tests in tests/test_migrate.py directly cover the regression scenario from ISSUE.md

settlement.rationale: All 5 declared criteria assessed supported with high confidence: rename, version bump, recursive preservation of unknown keys (incl. nested, independently copied), no mutation of input, and 3 new regression tests added. Not settling as 'land' since committing/merging was not requested; the fix remains uncommitted in the working tree pending user direction.
